display.title: Tanya Shiur 29: Shivisi Hashem L'negdi Tamid and Tanya Chapter 13 (Elul)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur: the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch on waking up before the King, Tanya chapter 13 on the beinoni, and an Elul talk on crowning Hashem on Rosh Hashanah.
display.summary_long: Shiur 29 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, recorded in Elul. Part 1 studies Shulchan Aruch HaRav, Hilchos Hashkamas HaBoker 1:4-5. On waking, one should think before Whom one lies: the King of kings stands over him, so he rises with alacrity, and 'Shivisi Hashem l'negdi tamid' is a great principle of the Torah. Stories illustrate it: the young Tzemach Tzedek in the Alter Rebbe's home, the Baal Shem Tov's father's words 'fear nothing but G-d', and Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakai's deathbed blessing that his students fear Heaven as much as they fear people. Part 2 continues Tanya chapter 13: the beinoni, in whom the yetzer tov and yetzer hara are both 'judges', and Hashem's help that lets the G-dly soul prevail. Part 3 is an Elul talk: Rosh Hashanah as accepting Hashem as King (malchiyos), illustrated with a mashal of a flame, a glowing coal and the fire hidden in a flint stone, and the Chassidic custom of taking stock of the year from Chai Elul.
display.lesson: Remember constantly that Hashem stands before you; that awareness brings alacrity, fear of Heaven and joy in serving Him.

date.note: Before Chai Elul; shiur 29b, a week later, is the day after Chai Elul 5736. Likely about 12 Elul.
